precepts.text: The bitings of flies killed and no remedy was found; these were no ordinary flies.
precepts.point: Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle; it was given to us in the days of Joseph, as we read in the book of Genesis.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

precepts.why:
These were no ordinary flies. “For them the bitings of grasshoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such.”

The swarms of flies were biting and killing men and animals, and no remedy was found; “the land was corrupted by reason of the swarm of flies.” The Egyptians were worthy to be punished by such, while the Lord severed the land of Goshen, where His people dwelt, so that no swarms of flies were there.

precepts.text: Manna was angels' food, agreeing to every taste and tempering itself to every man's liking.
precepts.point: The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
precepts.why:
“And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium”, gathered, ground, baked in pans, “and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.” Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised.

“Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels’ food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.” Manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up when it fell with the dew in the night.

“For thy sustenance declared thy sweetness unto thy children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.” It was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for.

To complain about that provision was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.

precepts.text: It is neither herb nor plaster that heals, but the word of the Most High, in whose hand is our healing.
precepts.point: Isaiah applies a lump of figs to the boil and Hezekiah recovers, showing that remedies and herbs go together with prayer, for healing is in the hand of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
“For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things.”

Isaiah said, “Take a lump of figs”, and they laid it on the boil, and Hezekiah recovered. Remedies and herbs go together with prayer. But it was not the figs that healed him. Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, and the word came, “I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee.”

It is neither herb nor plaster that heals, but the word of the Most High. Our healing is in his hand.

precepts.text: In the wilderness the angels' food agreed to every taste, whatever your delight was it tasted like, yet we still complained as a people.
precepts.point: They draw near unto the gates of death, then they cry unto the Lord in their trouble and He saveth them. He sent His word and healed them, so we get healed today by God's word.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Their soul abhorreth all manner of meat; and they draw near unto the gates of death.” In the wilderness the Most High “feddest thine own people with angels’ food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.”

The angels' food agreed to every taste: whatever your delight was, it tasted like that. Yet we still complained as a people, and our soul abhorred all manner of meat. That shows how stiffnecked we were even in the wilderness, and why the Bible calls us fools who are afflicted because of our transgression and our iniquities.

precepts.text: They were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.
precepts.point: The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Solomon tells what the serpent of brass was: “For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever: But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.”

The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. They were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it. They had said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord”, and the sign put them in remembrance of the commandment of the law.

So when the Son of man is lifted up like that serpent, believing in him goes with the same thing: remembrance of the commandment of the law, and repentance.

precepts.text: It is the word of the Most High that healeth all things, so the word is what restores our people to health.
precepts.point: We cannot heal a body today, but we heal every day with the word: drug dealers, baby mothers, and survivors of mental, physical, alcoholic, drug, and religious abuse are healed when they receive the truth. When people say we do not feed the poor, the truth is the poor have the gospel preached to them, and that is the healing.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things.” It is the word of the Most High that heals all things.

Peter lifted the lame man and his feet and ankle bones received strength. We cannot do that with a body today, but the word restores our people to health: the healing of the mind and the life, when the truth is received.
